environment.setup: One frozen copyfile install, installer reported 9.57 seconds for 923 packages; excluded from every paired command. Tests import live TypeScript. Command wall/CPU/RSS include wrapper, preload and module load. Per-case bodies exclude those costs.

mapping: All original 15 case names remain in order, with all original error/status/resource/capacity expectations retained. Original full-file count: 82; candidate: 184 including teardown and the added failure-path control.
Queue expiry is asserted before releasing the held slot; just-before/due registration checks precede its original error assertion.

Acquisition and page creation/rendering retain separate timers; the 80+80 ms success is driven across logical 160 ms and its 120 ms rendering allowance starts after acquisition. Cleared acquisition/render timers stay retired beyond their prior deadlines.
Overlapping acquisition and render cases start the second call 50/70 logical ms later. Their actual pending timers remain independent as the first expires; the newer timer clears on success.
Idle closes at 30 logical ms after completion, remains absent during capture, relaunches and clears/rearms when a new render starts.

Late launch, page and content resolution drains real promise jobs via a native event-loop turn before original close/configuration/capture assertions. Removing all expiration guards fails the original screenshots == 0 assertion.
Wedged page close remains detached. Browser cleanup registers 2000, remains pending at 1999 and finishes at 2000 logical ms; the outer 2500 ms failure ceiling remains native.

Cleanup after a synthetic failure drives real registered callbacks, checks no pending timers and restores complete global descriptors in finally. No public injection seam or production change. This scheduling proof makes no native Chrome duration claim.
